newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to issue treasury bonds this month.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to issue treasury bonds this month.

text.p: Sri Lanka will start issuing treasury bonds from February 27 as a first step towards developing a long-term debt market, a senior Central Bank official told Reuters on Wednesday.
"We will start with a two-year Treasury Bond. The first auction is on February 27, and the issue on March 3," said the official who declined to be identified.
Auctions are to be held every two weeks for 500 million rupees a time, with interest based on a coupon rate of 15 percent. The issues will be underwritten by the state-run Employees Provident Fund.

The Central Bank first floated the idea of issuing Treasury Bonds in mid-1996, but was unable to launch them due to infrastructure problems resulting from the January 1996 bomb attack on its head office, officials said.
Analysts in Sri Lanka, which has long suffered from a lack of transferable long-term securities, said the move would stabilise interest rates.
"It is good to see that the government is starting to cut its dependence on short-term debt, because it will also help to stabilise interest rates," said Azra Jafferjee, economist at Jardine Fleming.

Sri Lanka has three-, six- and 12-month Treasury Bills which are traded in the secondary market. Government securities of two-year, five to six-year and seven- to eight-year maturities are not usually traded as they are mostly issued to government institutions.
